what_it_does: An AHA exfoliant that smooths texture, brightens tone, and can help hydrate skin.
summary_short: Lactic acid is a water-soluble alpha hydroxy acid used to gently exfoliate the skin’s surface. It can improve dullness, uneven texture, and discoloration, while being somewhat more hydrating than some other AHAs.
summary_long:
Lactic acid is an alpha hydroxy acid (AHA). In skincare, it works mainly by loosening the bonds between dead skin cells on the surface, helping them shed more evenly. This can make skin look smoother, brighter, and less flaky over time.

Compared with some other exfoliating acids, lactic acid is often considered a gentler AHA because it has a larger molecular size than glycolic acid and also has water-binding properties. That means it can support smoother-feeling skin while still being less aggressive than stronger exfoliating routines.

The provided research is mostly about lactic acid in vaginal health, fermentation, and industrial production rather than topical skincare. One review describes lactic acid as an acidifying molecule with antimicrobial and immune-related effects in the vaginal environment [PMID:unknown], but that does not directly prove the same benefits for facial skincare. For cosmetic use, the strongest practical takeaway is its well-established role as a surface exfoliant.

In over-the-counter skincare, lactic acid is commonly found in lower-strength leave-on products and higher-strength peels. Higher concentrations and lower pH formulas are more likely to sting, cause redness, or disrupt the skin barrier, especially for sensitive skin.

Use carefully with other exfoliants, retinoids, benzoyl peroxide, or strong vitamin C products, since combining too many active ingredients can increase irritation. Daily sunscreen is important when using AHAs because exfoliated skin can be more vulnerable to sun-related discoloration and sensitivity.
